answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a refundable bond before bidding for wharf delivery jobs. The bond stays frozen for a 30-day horizon after the last job, and signed proof of non-delivery triggers forfeiture. This makes the bond a signal of capital at risk, not proof of identity: an attacker can create many names, but each active name needs fresh collateral, so multiplying identities multiplies locked capital and potential losses.
